I've published over 15 apps with AI, and these two things were caught in almost all of them.  The first one is likely why your app is laggy.  When setting up the server, your coding agent probably built the app to ask the server  for data every few seconds forever.  This is called polling.  This might feel fine during testing, but when users actually try the app, it'll  drain their battery and lower their framerate.  Nowadays, modern backends like SuperBase or Convex can actually push data directly to  your app when it changes.  So make sure your AI is not polling, but rather subscribing to events as they happen.  The second one can explain why your AI actually keeps going in circles and breaking things.  Every time you request a change, most AIs don't actually change it.  Rather, they create a version 2 on top of the broken version 1, just in case anybody  was using it.  This causes your app to be full of broken code that nobody was using anyway.  Now for your future prompts, the AI will get confused between which is the working  version and now go in circles and break things that seem to be working before.  To fix this, just tell it not to use fallbacks or backwards compatibility.  Just replace the old feature and make sure the new one works.
